title: Alternating Lying Leg Raise
overview: The Alternating Lying Leg Raise is a core exercise that strengthens the lower abdominal muscles and improves hip mobility. Lifting one leg at a time reduces strain on the lower back and enhances control compared todouble-leg raises.
instructions: Lie flat on your back with arms at your sides and legs straight. You can also put your hands underneath your lower back for support.
Engage your core and press your lower back into the floor. This is the starting position.
Slowly lift one leg off the ground until it's about 45–60 degrees from the floor (or as high as flexibility allows). Keep the other leg extended and relaxed on the floor.
Lower the working leg slowly. This is one rep.
tips: Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
Move slowly and with control to maximize core engagement.
Avoid arching your back. If your lower back lifts off the floor, limit your range of motion or bend your knees slightly.
For added difficulty, hover the resting leg slightly off the ground instead of laying it fully down.
